jobs.description_text: Available Location: Singapore Why This Role Exists Cloudflare built its reputation helping build a better Internet, defending millions of sites, giving away SSL and DDoS mitigation when the industry charged premium prices. In an acceleratingly dangerous world, the scope of that mission has changed. We are becoming something more: critical infrastructure. Banks run their payment rails on us. Governments run public services on us. Media companies depend on us during live events. Health systems depend on us to provide care. Reliability for these customers is no longer a feature of our product. It is a mission. Serving that customer base demands a different operating model. Traditional support organizations route tickets. Traditional engineering organizations ship features. Neither alone is enough when the stakes are this high. We are pivoting to something different: a customer-facing engineering organization, directly engaged with our customers at scale. This is work a central dev team cannot do from the inside of the network. The Customer Reliability Engineering function is the spine of that pivot. CRE is SRE applied outward, the same engineering discipline, applied to the reliability of the systems our customers run on Cloudflare. jobs.title: Model Operations Lead, AI Gateway
jobs.description_text: Available Locations: Austin, TX | New York City, NY | San Francisco, CA About AI Gateway AI inference is becoming core infrastructure. Every serious application will need access to many models across many providers, with reliability, observability, security, cost control, and routing built in from the start. AI Gateway is Cloudflare's bet that this layer belongs at the network edge: close to users, close to compute, and simple enough that a developer can adopt it with one API change. Developers using AI Gateway need answers to two questions. Is the model I'm calling working the way you say it does? And which model should I be using at all? You'll lead the models team that answers both. You'll start with model operations. That's the work behind every model in the catalog: provider integrations, capability testing, pricing and metering, capacity, security reviews, docs, health, and deprecations. Sometimes a launch needs to go live within minutes of a lab's announcement. Sometimes the right call is to hold it. Cloudflare is an infrastructure company at heart, so reliability and accuracy come first; speed comes from preparation and automation. Then you'll bring model intelligence online. That means turning what we learn from Gateway traffic into decisions for customers: capability maps, per-task rankings, auto-routing profiles that pick the right model for each request, evals and regression detection, and market intelligence developers can trust. This is a people-management role

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Certificate Authority
jobs.description_text: Available Locations: Austin or London About the Role TLS is the connective tissue of the Internet, and Cloudflare terminates a large fraction of it. Cloudflare sits in front of more than 20 percent of global Internet request traffic and terminates TLS for millions of domains. Every day, our network handles certificate operations across products like Universal SSL, SSL for SaaS, Origin CA, Cloudflare Access, and Cloudflare Tunnel. That scale has taught us how the WebPKI ecosystem works from the consuming side. As certificate lifetimes shorten, agentic activity increases, and post-quantum certificates move toward production, the number of certificates the Internet depends on will grow dramatically. Cloudflare is building a certificate authority for the whole Internet: a public, redundant, transparent CA that provides another trusted source of automated certificates and helps make the encrypted web more resilient. We intend to be ACME-first, automation-first, and transparent by design. We also intend to lead where the ecosystem is going, including post-quantum certificates and Merkle Tree Certificates, while continuing to support the classic WebPKI customers rely on today. As Principal Product Manager for Cloudflare's Certificate Authority business, you will define the product strategy, roadmap, customer experience, and commercial model for this new venture. You will work across product, engineering, security, compliance, legal, operations, sales, marketing, and the WebPKI ecosy

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Agentic Search
jobs.description_text: Locations: Austin, Lisbon, San Francisco, NYC, or London About the Role Search is being rebuilt around AI. People increasingly get answers from AI instead of a list of links, agents run dozens of searches to answer a single question, and more than half of the traffic reaching sites on Cloudflare is now automated . Search is shifting from a destination to a utility, and Cloudflare is building the search layer for this agentic Internet. Agentic Search at Cloudflare gives agents everything they need to find information, whether it lives in a customer’s own data or on the open web. It spans two products: AI Search for internal data, and Web Search API for the open web. AI Search (internal data), now generally available , is the search primitive for applications and agents . It is a fully managed indexing and retrieval pipeline built on Workers AI , Vectorize , R2 , and Browser Run . Developers connect a website or R2 bucket, or upload their own files, and query them with natural language through a Workers binding, REST API, or MCP server. Under the hood: continuous indexing, hybrid vector and keyword retrieval, reranking, metadata filtering, native multimodal (image) embeddings, and OCR for scanned documents. We use it to power search on our own blog and developer docs. Web Search API (external data), now in open beta , gives agents real-time web context with a single API call. It runs on AI Gateway , so every search gets the same logging, analytics, billing, and access controls

jobs.description_text: Available Locations: London, New York City, Denver, Lisbon, Seattle, or Austin About the Role Millions of websites, applications, APIs, and AI agents run on Cloudflare, and the traffic we handle for them produces a lot of data. Some customers want to debug applications and investigate security events in Cloudflare. Others want that data in a stack they already trust, such as Splunk, Datadog, Grafana, or their own data lake. Many want both. We're hiring one Senior Product Manager for each of two areas. You apply once, and we'll work out together which role fits you best. Observability Platform brings logs, traces, analytics, alerts, and dashboards together in one place, so customers can see what's happening and why. Today most observability ends with a notification, and the customer does the rest. We want a platform that understands the problem, takes action where it can, and asks before doing anything risky. Telemetry Export delivers Cloudflare's data to the tools customers choose. Logpush handles most of that delivery today, and Workers Observability sends logs and traces over the OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP). Customers want OTLP for the rest of Cloudflare's data, metrics pushed to their own tools, and a way to send us telemetry from workloads that run elsewhere. Your mission is to make reliability and security something customers rarely have to worry about, with the data they need in Cloudflare or in the tools they already use. That knowledge came from watching how humans moved through the web. Agents break that loop. AI models are trained and grounded on the web, but they have little visibility into what's changed, what's authoritative, or what's been fabricated. Site owners have it worse: AI crawlers already request content anywhere from a hundred to tens of thousands of times for every visitor they send back, and most have no idea how, or whether, they show up in AI answers. Both sides of the market are flying blind. Cloudflare sits in front of around 20% of the web and sees both sides of that exchange. Our team, the Agentic Internet team, is focused on making the web readable, discoverable, callable, and payable, built on open standards so no single company owns the rails. Signals & Data Products turns our network's view into products both sides can use: helping AI labs know what's fresh and trustworthy, and helping site owners see and shape how they show up in AI. Cloudflare believes in the open Internet, and we're in a position to help build the future where it thrives. Come help us make it happen! You can read more about some of our plans here and here . jobs.title: Systems Engineer - Network Data Plane Software
jobs.description_text: Locations: Austin TX, Champaign IL, Lisbon Portugal, London England, Atlanta GA, Washington DC, About the team Cloudflare is redefining the way networks are run at scale, and some of the largest networks in the world now run their traffic through us. Cloudflare's network runs in hundreds of cities on general-purpose Linux servers, not dedicated routers, so the routers, firewalls, load balancers, and proxies that carry our customers' traffic are software that we write, ship, and operate ourselves. Our Packet Processing team builds and operates that software: high-performance code that processes customer traffic at the packet level as it moves through Cloudflare's network, in every Cloudflare data center. That includes the L4 load balancer at the front door of every server, a per-customer routing and forwarding data plane, a stateful network firewall, and a TCP/UDP reverse proxy (the engines behind products like Magic Transit, Cloudflare WAN, Cloudflare Network Firewall, and Spectrum). We are a team of engineers who obsess over performance, correctness, and reliability at massive scale. We own what we build in production, a lot of our work happens close to the kernel and the NIC. About the role We're looking for engineers who want to build the software that forwards, filters, and load-balances packets for a meaningful fraction of the internet. jobs.title: Developer Advocate
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THIS ROLE Developers decide what infrastructure wins. They try three platforms in an afternoon, keep the one that got them to a working inference call fastest, and tell everyone else about it. As a Developer Advocate at Fireworks, you own a piece of that decision: you make Fireworks the platform developers reach for first when they want to build, fine-tune, and serve frontier open models in production. You do that by building things worth showing, not by talking about things other people built. This role has a dual bar, and we mean both halves of it. You are a working engineer: you ship code, read diffs, deploy models, and can hold your own in a conversation about batching, quantization, or why a fine-tune regressed. You are also a public technical communicator: you write clearly enough that a senior engineer forwards it, you're good on a stage, and you have or want a real presence in the places developers actually argue about this stuff. Most people are strong at one and passable at the other. We're looking for the rarer profile who is genuinely credible at both, because in AI infrastructure the audience can tell within one paragraph whether you've actually run the thing. The field moves weekly. A major open-weights model drops and the window to be the definitive resource on it is measured in days. jobs.description_text: The Role: Make data a solved problem for every GPU workload at Fireworks.
